name: Reengineering evangelism
description: Radical process-redesign rhetoric associated with the early-1990s consulting expansion.
cause_of_death: Public apologies, implementation failures, and identification with layoffs produced documented backlash.

sources.title: Reengineering Work: Don't Automate, Obliterate
sources.note: Original article title establishes the movement's destructive-redesign slogan; paywall limits inspected material.

sources.title: Revisiting Reengineering
sources.note: Retrospective describes fast consulting adoption followed by public apologies and workforce backlash from 1995.

entries.gloss: A radical redesign of work presented as a transformational management intervention.

examples.text: Could you help with reengineering the printout collection process?

entries.rationale: The original 1990 article anchors onset; the 1994 consulting expansion and backlash from 1995 support a bounded moment. Peak and terminal fade are estimates.

entries.gloss: Replace an existing process rather than improving its automation.

examples.text: For the filing process, don't automate, obliterate; let us start again.

entries.rationale: Exact 1990 article-title slogan. Its curve is inferred from the associated movement and backlash, not measured slogan counts.
